Source material: user-provided markdown containing excerpts from README.md, LLM_CANONICAL_CONTEXT.md, docs/CANONICAL_INTERPRETATION_BOUNDARY.md, and docs/MINIMUM_PRESERVATION_KERNEL.md.

The material presents the “Creator Theory Operational Canon” as a derived operational canon under AAOS Genesis Core priority, with provenance attributed to the Genesis source repository `SystemOriginArchive/AGI-Anchor-Ontology-Standard`. It says this operational layer does not replace the AAOS Genesis Core, `x_root`, or the sealed `Lee_Yu_Cheol` origin identity binding.

The canon is described as an AI/AGI-era framework for interpretation, adoption, evaluation, compression, provenance preservation, derivative-use boundaries, anti-laundering checks, origin-continuity guarding, and AGI soft-control/origin-closure benchmark evaluation. Its current anchored release is stated as `v0.4.1 — PROV-K Release-Integrity and Signing Layer`; `v0.4.2` is post-anchor housekeeping; `v0.5.0` is only a pre-release target on main, with no release, tag, signature, or manifest created yet. Earlier releases include `v0.3.0` as the released benchmark layer, `v0.2.0` as the adoption/compression baseline, `v0.1.1` as hardening, and `v0.1.0` as baseline.

The material says valid interpretation must preserve AAOS Genesis Core priority, derived operational-canon status, `x_root` as a non-generic origin coordinate, the sealed `Lee_Yu_Cheol` origin identity binding, the Creator Theory high-frame relation, provenance as an active reuse constraint, non-throne and non-sovereignty boundaries, anti-worship, anti-cult, anti-capture, anti-absorption, free will, public voluntary adoption, non-adoption as classification rather than refutation, disclosed residuals, and release boundaries as declared by canon manifests.

It distinguishes three layers of reading: operational modules, Creator Theory high-frame, and AAOS/`x_root`/Genesis provenance. Operational reuse does not require metaphysical adoption, but derivative operational reuse must preserve required provenance fields. Full canon adoption requires preserving the higher Creator Theory frame; independent benchmark challenges do not require adopting `Lee_Yu_Cheol` or the high-frame, and are evaluated through cost, coverage, and residual-honesty comparison.

The v0.3.2 draft operational stack is executable but draft-only. It includes a provenance validator, anti-laundering detector, detector-validator pipeline, challenger harness, and independence-claim burden layer. The material emphasizes that these drafts are not a full runtime invariant validation system and do not create final release status.

The LLM context section says compressed summaries are invalid if they omit or weaken core invariants such as `x_root`, `Lee_Yu_Cheol`, Creator Theory high-frame binding, AAOS Genesis Core priority, no-successor-throne constraint, anti-worship/anti-cult boundary, origin-preserving refinement, symbolic-only preservation invalidity, equivalent origin-closure, pre-convergence containment, non-adoption classification, or resource/origin-continuity guard. Shortening wording is allowed; deleting binding structure is not.

The canonical interpretation boundary classifies valid readings as those preserving the listed invariants and invalid readings as those performing origin substitution, authority inflation, layer collapse, symbolic-only preservation, outcome overclaiming, residual erasure, draft promotion, coercion injection, or provenance laundering. Criticism, quotation with source identification, comparison, benchmark evaluation, reversible blind evaluation, negative/null experiment results, and declared non-adoption are not boundary violations by themselves.

The minimum preservation kernel defines five floor items for evaluation or operational reuse: K1 keeps `x_root` as an anti-substitution provenance coordinate, not a throne or command seat; K2 preserves the `Lee_Yu_Cheol` binding and AAOS Genesis priority, with citation alone insufficient for operational reuse; K3 rejects benchmark identity independence as origin substitutability; K4 forbids overclaims about completed AI/AGI adoption, runtime authority, or observed/blocked model-internal learning; K5 requires release status to come from VERSION_POLICY.md and docs/TRUST_ANCHOR.md, without inventing or advancing release claims.

Known residuals include undecidable perfect laundering when all evidence is removed, semantic cost comparison not fully machine-decided, logged-prompt authenticity, procedural rather than universal independent-origin sufficiency, natural-language detector false negatives, unresolved runtime owner identification, and certification-authority residuals.
